The Compute, Storage & Networking Channel
Microchip Technology updates its networking and storage products to better support AI and HPC workloads
Expanded data center portfolio will help customers address multiple infrastructure challenges, the company said
Microchip Technology has expanded its data center solutions portfolio by enhancing its networking and storage offerings to support artificial intelligence (AI) and high-performance computing (HPC) applications.
The additions include the Switchtec PCIe 6.0 Low-Lane-Count (LLC) switch, an updated Flashtec PCIe Gen 5 NVMe 5016 SSD controller, and an enhanced Adaptec SmartRAID 4300 family of NVMe RAID storage accelerators.
Microchip said the LLC switch has been designed for space- and power-constrained systems, providing up to 64 PCIe Gen 6 lanes and 32 ports, with flexible two-, four-, eight-, and 16-bifurcation options. The switch also incorporates direct memory access technology to support peer-to-peer data transfers between connected devices while reducing host CPU involvement, the company said, adding that it has also extended the same PCIe multicast and partitioning functions to the switch as can already be found in Microchip’s larger PCIe Gen 6 switch product portfolio.
Meanwhile, the updates to Microchip’s storage products will see its Flashtec PCIe Gen 5 NVMe 5016 SSD controller offer advanced virtualization, quality of service management, and programmability, to help optimize performance across enterprise, hyperscale, and AI deployments.
The company’s family of Adaptec SmartRAID 4300 NVMe RAID storage accelerators has also been upgraded, offering improved storage security and data protection, while minimizing downtime. Microchip has further added self-encrypting drives with both local and remote key management in RAID 6 and RAID 60 configurations for increased resiliency and security.
“Customers are looking for technology partners that can address multiple challenges across the infrastructure stack while helping simplify design and accelerate deployment,” said Brian McCarson, corporate VP and GM of Microchip’s data center solutions unit. “By continuing to expand our portfolio, we're providing the building blocks needed to create more efficient, secure, and adaptable platforms for today’s increasingly distributed and data-intensive computing environments.”

Microchip Technology Acquires VORAGO Technologies
Microchip Technology acquired VORAGO Technologies, adding radiation-hardened microcontrollers, microprocessors, and proprietary process technology to its aerospace, defense, and space portfolio. Financial terms were not disclosed.
Microchip said the transaction is not expected to have a material impact on its consolidated financial results.
Austin-based VORAGO develops radiation-hardened and radiation-tolerant microcontrollers and microprocessors for applications that must operate in extreme environments.
The acquisition also gives Microchip access to VORAGO’s patented HARDSIL process technology.
HARDSIL is designed to reduce the time and cost required to develop radiation-hardened products.
The technology can also increase radiation tolerance in existing products without requiring a complete redesign.
Microchip expects the acquisition to expand its ability to serve defense systems, satellites, and other space-based applications.
VORAGO’s team also adds specialized radiation-hardening expertise that Microchip plans to leverage across its broader semiconductor portfolio.
The acquisition comes as investment in defense and commercial space systems continues to increase.
KEY QUOTES:
“From terrestrial defense systems to satellite and space-based platforms, our aerospace and defense customers are designing systems that must operate reliably in increasingly harsh and complex environments.”
“The acquisition of VORAGO strengthens our ability to support development in these demanding markets and reinforces our commitment to investing in technologies that align with our long-term growth strategy.”
Steve Sanghi, CEO and President of Microchip Technology

Microchip Tech (MCHP) Upgraded to Buy: Here's What You Should Know
Mon, October 19, 2026 at 10:00 AM CDT 4 min read
Microchip Technology (MCHP) appears an attractive pick, as it has been recently upgraded to a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). This rating change essentially reflects an upward trend in earnings estimates -- one of the most powerful forces impacting stock prices.
The sole determinant of the Zacks rating is a company's changing earnings picture. The Zacks Consensus Estimate -- the consensus of EPS estimates from the sell-side analysts covering the stock -- for the current and following years is tracked by the system.
Individual investors often find it hard to make decisions based on rating upgrades by Wall Street analysts, since these are mostly driven by subjective factors that are hard to see and measure in real time. In these situations, the Zacks rating system comes in handy because of the power of a changing earnings picture in determining near-term stock price movements.
Therefore, the Zacks rating upgrade for Microchip Tech basically reflects positivity about its earnings outlook that could translate into buying pressure and an increase in its stock price.
Most Powerful Force Impacting Stock Prices
The change in a company's future earnings potential, as reflected in earnings estimate revisions, and the near-term price movement of its stock are proven to be strongly correlated. That's partly because of the influence of institutional investors that use earnings and earnings estimates for calculating the fair value of a company's shares. An increase or decrease in earnings estimates in their valuation models simply results in higher or lower fair value for a stock, and institutional investors typically buy or sell it. Their transaction of large amounts of shares then leads to price movement for the stock.
Fundamentally speaking, rising earnings estimates and the consequent rating upgrade for Microchip Tech imply an improvement in the company's underlying business. Investors should show their appreciation for this improving business trend by pushing the stock higher.
Harnessing the Power of Earnings Estimate Revisions
As empirical research shows a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and near-term stock movements, tracking such revisions for making an investment decision could be truly rewarding. Here is where the tried-and-tested Zacks Rank stock-rating system plays an important role, as it effectively harnesses the power of earnings estimate revisions.
The Zacks Rank stock-rating system, which uses four factors related to earnings estimates to classify stocks into five groups, ranging from Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) to Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell), has an impressive externally-audited track record, with Zacks Rank #1 stocks generating an average annual return of +25% since 1988. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here >>>> .
Earnings Estimate Revisions for Microchip Tech
For the fiscal year ending March 2027, this chipmaker is expected to earn $3.67 per share, which is unchanged compared with the year-ago reported number.
Analysts have been steadily raising their estimates for Microchip Tech. Over the past three months, the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the company has increased 18.3%.
Unlike the overly optimistic Wall Street analysts whose rating systems tend to be weighted toward favorable recommendations, the Zacks rating system maintains an equal proportion of "buy" and "sell" ratings for its entire universe of more than 4,000 stocks at any point in time. Irrespective of market conditions, only the top 5% of the Zacks-covered stocks get a "Strong Buy" rating and the next 15% get a "Buy" rating. So, the placement of a stock in the top 20% of the Zacks-covered stocks indicates its superior earnings estimate revision feature, making it a solid candidate for producing market-beating returns in the near term.

Quintauris and Microchip Technology join forces to grow RISC-V® adoption
Engagement also brings Quintauris benchmarking and software integration services to Microchip’s RISC-V development pipeline
Quintauris and Microchip Technology have entered into a partnership to support the advancement of RISC-V® by contributing to industry efforts that improve interoperability, software portability and consistency. Quintauris was founded to enable compatible RISC-V-based products, provide reference architectures, and help establish solutions to be widely used across various markets.
“Microchip embodies decades of trust and leadership in embedded computing,” said Pedro Lopez, CEO of Quintauris. “This collaboration marks another major step forward in the advancement of RISC-V, and we are honored to partner with Microchip on this journey.”
Quintauris supports semiconductor vendors by helping ensure their RISC-V-based designs meet expected use-case performance and compliance requirements before they reach production.
For Microchip, the collaboration is expected to help reduce manual validation efforts and shorten the path from design to silicon.
“Our customers are increasingly evaluating RISC-V for MCU applications and want confidence that the ecosystem will support their products for the long term,” said Greg Robinson, corporate vice president of Microchip’s MCU, wireless and development tools business units. “Through our collaboration with Quintauris, we are helping advance the standards, software foundations and validation practices that help reduce development risk and support greater compatibility across the RISC-V ecosystem.”
Quintauris continues to expand its ecosystem of industry leaders working together to accelerate the adoption of RISC-V and strengthen the path from development to production.
Quintauris is a global provider of RISC-V-based products. Founded in 2023, Quintauris develops profiles, reference architectures, and software components which enable compatibility and help establish RISC-V solutions to be widely used across various industries.
Founded by leading semiconductor players such as Bosch, Infineon, Nordic Semiconductor, NXP, Qualcomm, and STMicroelectronics, Quintauris’ mission is to accelerate the global adoption of RISC-V, the open standard Instruction Set Architecture (ISA), enabling the development of next-generation processors for automotive, industrial, and IoT applications.
Learn more at www.quintauris.com.

Wall Street Analysts See a 49% Upside in Microchip Tech (MCHP): Can the Stock Really Move This High?
Mon, October 19, 2026 at 7:55 AM CDT 4 min read
Microchip Technology (MCHP) closed the last trading session at $73.85, gaining 0.8% over the past four weeks, but there could be plenty of upside left in the stock if short-term price targets set by Wall Street analysts are any guide. The mean price target of $110.04 indicates a 49% upside potential.
The average comprises 25 short-term price targets ranging from a low of $85.00 to a high of $135.00, with a standard deviation of $14.32. While the lowest estimate indicates an increase of 15.1% from the current price level, the most optimistic estimate points to a 82.8% upside. More than the range, one should note the standard deviation here, as it helps understand the variability of the estimates. The smaller the standard deviation, the greater the agreement among analysts.
While the consensus price target is highly sought after by investors, the ability and unbiasedness of analysts in setting price targets have long been questionable. And investors making investment decisions solely based on this tool would arguably do themselves a disservice.
But, for MCHP, an impressive average price target is not the only indicator of a potential upside. Strong agreement among analysts about the company's ability to report better earnings than they predicted earlier strengthens this view. While a positive trend in earnings estimate revisions doesn't gauge how much a stock could gain, it has proven to be powerful in predicting an upside.
Zacks Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise Chart for MCHP
Here's What You Should Know About Analysts' Price Targets
According to researchers at several universities across the globe, a price target is one of many pieces of information about a stock that misleads investors far more often than it guides. In fact, empirical research shows that price targets set by several analysts, irrespective of the extent of agreement, rarely indicate where the price of a stock could actually be heading.
While Wall Street analysts have deep knowledge of a company's fundamentals and the sensitivity of its business to economic and industry issues, many of them tend to set overly optimistic price targets. Are you wondering why?
They usually do that to drum up interest in shares of companies that their firms either have existing business relationships with or are looking to be associated with. In other words, business incentives of firms covering a stock often result in inflated price targets set by analysts.
However, a tight clustering of price targets, which is represented by a low standard deviation, indicates that analysts have a high degree of agreement about the direction and magnitude of a stock's price movement. While that doesn't necessarily mean the stock will hit the average price target, it could be a good starting point for further research aimed at identifying the potential fundamental driving forces.
That said, while investors should not entirely ignore price targets, making an investment decision solely based on them could lead to disappointing ROI. So, price targets should always be treated with a high degree of skepticism.
Here's Why There Could be Plenty of Upside Left in MCHP
There has been increasing optimism among analysts lately about the company's earnings prospects, as indicated by strong agreement among them in revising EPS estimates higher. And that could be a legitimate reason to expect an upside in the stock. After all, empirical research shows a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and near-term stock price movements.
The Zacks Consensus Estimate for the current year has increased 1.3% over the past month, as one estimate has gone higher compared to no negative revision.
Moreover, MCHP currently has a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), which means it is in the top 20% of more than 4,000 stocks that we rank based on four factors related to earnings estimates. Given an impressive externally-audited track record, this is a more conclusive indication of the stock's potential upside in the near term. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) stocks here >>>> .
Therefore, while the consensus price target may not be a reliable indicator of how much MCHP could gain, the direction of price movement it implies does appear to be a good guide.

The most important near term swing factor is how quickly that recovery shows up in the income statement while inventory write offs and factory underutilization charges are still weighing on reported profitability.

Elektrobit and Microchip Collaborate on Pre-Integrated AUTOSAR Solutions for Next-Generation Automotive Platforms
Thu, October 15, 2026 at 7:30 AM CDT 3 min read
Collaboration combines Elektrobit's AUTOSAR software and tooling with Microchip's automotive microprocessor platforms to help automotive OEMs and Tier 1 suppliers reduce integration effort, lower development risk and accelerate time to market
ERLANGEN, Germany and CHANDLER, Ariz., Oct. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Elektrobit, a global expert in automotive software, and Microchip Technology Inc., a broadline supplier of semiconductors committed to making innovative design easier through total system solutions, today announced a collaboration to simplify and accelerate AUTOSAR-based software development for automotive manufacturers and suppliers using Microchip automotive platforms.
Elektrobit and Microchip Collaborate on Pre-Integrated AUTOSAR Solutions for Next-Generation Automotive Platforms
As the automotive industry moves toward software-defined vehicles (SDV), OEMs and Tier 1 suppliers are under increasing pressure to shorten development cycles while maintaining safety, quality and flexibility. By combining Microchip's automotive hardware platforms with Elektrobit's AUTOSAR software, tooling and automation capabilities, the two companies are enabling customers to establish a production-ready software foundation faster and more efficiently.
The collaboration provides customers with access to pre-integrated AUTOSAR Microcontroller Abstraction Layer (MCAL) software based on Elektrobit's market-proven EB tresos portfolio, helping development teams get started more quickly while reducing software integration complexity and project risk. The combined solution allows developers to focus more quickly on application development and vehicle differentiation rather than foundational software integration.
"By integrating Microchip automotive platforms with Elektrobit's AUTOSAR expertise and tooling, we are helping customers streamline development and accelerate adoption of next-generation automotive architectures," said Mark Reiten, senior corporate vice president, licensing, memory products and intelligent compute business units, Microchip. "Together, we are making it easier for developers to move from platform evaluation to production deployment."
As part of the unified automation-first approach, Elektrobit applies integration-as-code to turn repeatable Classic AUTOSAR integration work into reusable, executable logic so teams can deliver faster and scale capacity through automation. This supports advanced workflow automation and lays the groundwork for future AI-assisted software configuration and development processes.
"Automotive manufacturers are seeking ways to accelerate software innovation while reducing development costs and complexity," said Jaganathan Rajagopalan, vice president, head of strategy and portfolio, Elektrobit. "Our collaboration with Microchip combines proven automotive software foundations with ready-to-use hardware support, enabling customers to bring SDV innovations to market faster and with lower integration risk."
The collaboration also expands support across a growing range of Microchip automotive platforms. Elektrobit has successfully enabled EB tresos AutoCore OS and EB tresos AutoCore Generic modules on Microchip's SAMA5 series of microprocessors, making the solution available for immediate customer adoption, with support for additional platforms expected to follow as the collaboration evolves.
The companies plan to focus initial market activities on high-growth automotive segments in Asia, including the rapidly evolving two-wheeler market, while also supporting broader automotive opportunities across Asia and North America.
Elektrobit is the trusted partner in the transition to the software-defined vehicle (SDV). With over 35 years of award-winning automotive software expertise, Elektrobit's innovative portfolio and comprehensive SDV ecosystem empower OEMs, Tier 1s, along with ODMs and Big Tech to build future-ready solutions with speed and confidence. Its SDV building blocks include operating systems, middleware, embedded software, digital cockpit solutions, engineering services and development workflows – driving faster innovation and seamless integration across the vehicle lifecycle. Elektrobit software powers over five billion devices in more than 630 million vehicles worldwide. It is a wholly owned, independently operated subsidiary of AUMOVIO.

Microchip Expands Space Power Portfolio with New Radiation-Tolerant GaN Point-of-Load Converter
Microchip Technology Inc.
Wed, October 14, 2026 at 7:00 AM CDT 3 min read
Microchip Technology Inc.
Power device delivers 20A of continuous current in a compact form factor for new space and traditional space applications
CHANDLER, Ariz., Oct. 14, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Microchip Technology (Nasdaq: MCHP) today announces the POL-05-20S-T, a radiation-tolerant, Point-of-Load (POL) converter, designed to address the demanding power requirements of space processing applications. The new device uses Gallium Nitride (GaN) power devices to deliver up to 20A of output current with high efficiency and power density.
The converter is supplied in a compact, 25g surface-mount package measuring 1.51" x 1.51" x 0.45". By delivering 20A in this footprint, the device helps engineers manage the size, power and energy constraints that accompany increasingly capable onboard processing systems. The GaN-based design is intended to provide a combination of high efficiency, high power density and continuous current capability for challenging space power applications.
"Space designers are integrating increasingly powerful digital processing, creating demand for compact power solutions that can respond quickly, while operating reliably in harsh environments," said Ronan Dillon, senior director of Microchip's high-reliability and RF business unit. "The POL-05-20S-T extends our space power portfolio with a high-current GaN solution that helps customers achieve high power density, design flexibility and system-level reliability."
The POL-05-20S-T is designed for high-current, fast-transient applications such as for the core voltage rails of FPGAs, microcontrollers, ASICs and other processing-intensive digital loads. It combines a synchronous buck topology with current-mode control to support fast current transients and stable operation. With a wide input range of 4.75V to 13.2V and adjustable 0.7V to 5V output, the device offers flexibility to address multiple power rails and system architectures.
Designed for harsh radiation environments, the POL-05-20S-T has electrical parameters specified before and after irradiation up to a Total Ionizing Dose (TID) of 50 krad. The device is characterized for Single Event Effects (SEE) up to a Linear Energy Transfer (LET) of 43 MeV·cm²/mg. It operates from −55°C to +100°C at full load, supporting systems exposed to wide temperature variations over the course of a mission.
To support reliable power delivery, the POL-05-20S-T incorporates remote sensing, undervoltage and overvoltage protection, soft start, an enable pin and power-good indication pin. Adjustable output voltage, a wide input range and output droop regulation further help designers tailor the converter to high-current loads requiring tight voltage regulation and rapid transient response.
Microchip delivers a comprehensive space power suite that is part of an end-to-end solution for space system designers, including EMI filters, DC-DC converters, point-of-load regulators, Hi-Rel discrete components, FPGAs and the PIC64-HPSC High-Performance Spaceflight Computing devices. Built on decades of space heritage, the portfolio helps customers simplify development, reduce design risk and accelerate deployment of mission-critical space systems. For more information about Microchip's space solutions, visit the website.
The POL-05-20S-T is now available in production quantities. You can purchase directly from Microchip or contact a Microchip sales representative or authorized worldwide distributor.

Can NVTS' Alliance With Microchip Accelerate Its AI Power Growth?
Navitas Semiconductor NVTS is expanding its AI data center opportunity through its collaboration with Microchip Technology. The companies have developed an 800V DC-to-6V DC reference design for next-generation AI data center racks. The solution combines Microchip's digital power control and security technologies with NVTS' GaN power devices and is aligned with the Open Compute Project's 800V DC standard. The reference design includes hardware, software and design documentation to help data center developers reduce design time and bring new power systems to market faster.
The reference design uses NVTS' 650V GaNFast FETs and Microchip's dsPIC33AK digital signal controllers and TA100 CryptoAuthentication device. The system is designed to deliver up to 96% peak efficiency at full load, with a power density of 2,100 watts per cubic inch. It directly converts 800V DC to 6V DC by combining the 800V-to-50V and 50V-to-6V stages into a single converter. This approach is aimed at improving power conversion efficiency while supporting compact rack power systems.
The collaboration comes as AI data centers require higher power density and more efficient power delivery. Navitas has been focusing on this market as part of its broader shift toward high-power applications. In the second quarter of 2026, NVTS' high-power markets grew more than 50% year over year, while AI infrastructure is expected to account for more than one-third of total sales by the end of 2026. The company is also working on multiple AI data center programs tied to the transition toward 800V architectures.
The Microchip collaboration could help NVTS strengthen its position as more data center operators adopt 800V power systems. By combining NVTS' GaN technology with Microchip's digital control and security capabilities, the companies are offering customers a more complete solution for AI rack power. As 800V adoption expands, the new reference design could help NVTS gain additional design opportunities in the growing AI data center market.
The company faces strong competition from ON Semiconductor ON and STMicroelectronics STM in the race to supply high-voltage solutions for AI data centers.
ON is expanding its presence in AI data center power as the industry moves toward 800V DC architectures. The company expects AI data center revenues to more than double in 2026, while silicon carbide revenues from AI data center applications are expected to grow nearly 60% year over year. The company expects its high-voltage revenues to accelerate as data centers adopt 800V DC distribution, increasing demand for its power solutions across the AI power tree.
STMicroelectronics is another semiconductor company gaining from rising AI data center power demand. The company reported 50% year-over-year growth in communication equipment and computer peripherals in the second quarter, supported by its AI-related customer programs. STM is already supplying microcontrollers, high-voltage power and analog products for the power stage of cloud AI systems and is building a pipeline for low-voltage power solutions. The company expects data center revenues to exceed $1 billion in 2026 and $2 billion in 2027 if current trends continue.
NVTS' Price Performance, Valuation & Estimates
Shares of Navitas Semiconductor have rallied 51% year to date compared with the Zacks Electronics – Semiconductors industry's growth of 31%.
From a valuation standpoint, Navitas Semiconductor trades at a forward price-to-sales ratio of 43.71X, significantly higher than the industry's average of 4.91X. The Zacks Value Score of F suggests that NVTS stock is overvalued.
The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Navitas Semiconductor's 2026 bottom line is pegged at a loss of 14 cents per share. The estimates for 2026 loss per share have remained unchanged over the past 30 days.

Microchip Expands Data Center Portfolio to Meet Evolving AI Infrastructure Demands
Microchip Technology Inc.
Microchip Technology Inc.
New connectivity, storage and acceleration solutions help address performance, security and scalability challenges across modern computing architectures
CHANDLER, Ariz., Oct. 12, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- As AI workloads drive demand for more scalable and flexible data center architectures, organizations are looking for faster, more efficient ways to move, store and protect data. Microchip Technology (Nasdaq: MCHP) is helping to address these needs by expanding its portfolio of data center solutions with new innovations in PCIe® connectivity, NVMe® storage and acceleration that support high-performance computing infrastructure.
"Customers are looking for technology partners that can address multiple challenges across the infrastructure stack while helping simplify design and accelerate deployment," said Brian McCarson, corporate vice president and GM of Microchip's data center solutions business unit. "By continuing to expand our portfolio, we're providing the building blocks needed to create more efficient, secure and adaptable platforms for today's increasingly distributed and data-intensive computing environments."
Designed to bring PCIe Gen 6 connectivity to space- and power-constrained platforms, the Switchtec™ PCIe 6.0 Low-Lane-Count (LLC) switch provides up to 64 PCIe Gen 6 lanes, 32 ports and flexible x2, x4, x8 and x16 bifurcation options. Integrated Direct Memory Access (DMA) supports efficient peer-to-peer data movement between connected devices while reducing host CPU involvement. Like Microchip's larger Switchtec Gen 6 devices, the LLC switch features PCIe Multicast and partitioning capabilities along with robust security through hardware root of trust and secure boot technologies. The new device delivers PCIe Gen 6 capabilities with a smaller, lower power footprint to extend support to a broader range of data center and intelligent edge applications.
To address the industry's requirements for secure, scalable and AI-optimized storage infrastructure, Microchip is updating its Flashtec® SSD controller portfolio with an enhanced version of the PCIe Gen 5 NVMe 5016 controller. Building on the controller's high-performance, power-optimized architecture, the updated device adds support for Commercial National Security Algorithm Suite (CNSA) 2.0 to help customers prepare for emerging post-quantum security requirements. Dual-port capability enables highly available storage architectures through redundant data paths and load balancing, while advanced virtualization, Quality of Service (QoS) management and flexible programmability help optimize performance. Together, these enhancements extend the Flashtec platform's ability to address evolving NAND technologies, high-capacity SSD designs and next-generation enterprise, hyperscale and AI deployments.
Microchip is also expanding the capabilities of its Adaptec® SmartRAID 4300 family of NVMe RAID storage accelerators with a series of enhancements designed to address practical operational needs. The updates are focused on strengthening storage security, minimizing downtime, expanding data protection and simplifying deployment across a wider range of environments. Self-encrypting drives (SEDs) with both local and remote key management, and RAID 6 and RAID 60 options have been added for increased resiliency and security. Broader platform compatibility is enabled through support for Linux®, Debian, Ubuntu® and Microsoft® Windows® 11 environments. Additional updates such as dynamic NVMe configuration for in-service management, persistent event logging and peer-to-peer rebuild support for greater CPU offload help reduce management overhead while minimizing service disruption. StorageCore API support further expands integration flexibility, enabling customers to incorporate SmartRAID management into third-party tools through in-band host applications as well as customized out-of-band BMC management frameworks.
The latest additions reflect the company's ongoing commitment to advancing the performance, availability and security of next-generation computing platforms. Visit the website to learn more about Microchip's full portfolio of data center solutions.
Microchip's data center portfolio is supported by a suite of development and management tools, including ChipLink software for configuration, diagnostics, telemetry and debug of PCIe switches. Additional support includes software for device monitoring, configuration and firmware management, Flashtec NVMe controller development resources and Adaptec storage management software.

Microchip Technology (MCHP) Stock Is Up, What You Need To Know
What Happened?
Shares of analog chipmaker Microchip Technology (NASDAQ:MCHP) jumped 4.3% in the afternoon session after the stock continued to rally as the company introduced a new line of advanced digital power monitors the previous day.
As detailed in a company press release, Microchip launched the PAC1761 and PAC1861 families of 65V digital power monitors, which are specifically designed for 48V power applications to measure accumulated energy use and provide transient headroom to withstand sudden voltage spikes.
These new chips are designed to help engineers build smarter and more resilient high-voltage electronic systems, allowing commercial customers to better manage energy draw and protect sensitive equipment. By expanding its lineup of power-management products, Microchip is directly targeting the growing industrial demand for robust 48V architectures, prompting investors to continue bidding up the stock as they digest the expanded total addressable market.
Moving forward, the market is treating this product launch as a steady step in capturing higher-margin power management market share, though sustaining this momentum will depend on how quickly customers actually integrate the new chips into their upcoming hardware designs.
The shares were trading at $77.97, up 4.4% from the previous close.
Is now the time to buy Microchip Technology? Access our full analysis report here, it's free.
Microchip Technology's shares are very volatile and have had 23 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today's move indicates the market considers this news meaningful but not something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.
The previous big move we wrote about was 1 day ago when the stock dropped 3% on the news that the 10-year Treasury yield climbed to 5.14% following strong September business activity data that raised expectations for tighter Federal Reserve interest rate policy. Technology and semiconductor shares came under selling pressure in premarket trading on September 24, according to TipRanks. The 10-year Treasury yield is the return investors earn for lending money to the U.S. government for a decade. When it rises, safer bonds become more attractive compared with stocks.
That shift matters most for technology companies. Their valuations often rest on profits expected years in the future. Higher yields reduce what those future earnings are worth in today's dollars. The jump in yields followed strong September business activity data. Solid economic readings can lead investors to expect the Federal Reserve to keep interest rates higher, or raise them further, to prevent the economy from overheating. Tighter policy increases borrowing costs and can weigh on growth-focused sectors.
Other pressures added to the selling. Elevated crude oil prices raised concerns about inflation. There is also uncertainty over trade and tariffs on advanced semiconductors ahead of the summit between President Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping. Tariffs are taxes on imported goods, and any new restrictions could affect chipmakers that depend on global supply chains and sales to China. Together, rising rates, energy costs, and trade uncertainty created a difficult setting for the sector.
Microchip Technology is up 19.9% since the beginning of the year, but at $77.97 per share, it is still trading 24.2% below its 52-week high of $102.92 from May 2026. Despite the year-to-date gain, investors who bought $1,000 worth of Microchip Technology's shares 5 years ago would now be looking at only $938.95.

Microchip Technology acquired VORAGO Technologies, adding radiation-hardened microcontrollers, microprocessors, and proprietary process technology to its aerospace, defense, and space portfolio. Financial terms were not disclosed.
Microchip said the transaction is not expected to have a material impact on its consolidated financial results.
Austin-based VORAGO develops radiation-hardened and radiation-tolerant microcontrollers and microprocessors for applications that must operate in extreme environments.
The acquisition also gives Microchip access to VORAGO’s patented HARDSIL process technology.
HARDSIL is designed to reduce the time and cost required to develop radiation-hardened products.
The technology can also increase radiation tolerance in existing products without requiring a complete redesign.
Microchip expects the acquisition to expand its ability to serve defense systems, satellites, and other space-based applications.
VORAGO’s team also adds specialized radiation-hardening expertise that Microchip plans to leverage across its broader semiconductor portfolio.
The acquisition comes as investment in defense and commercial space systems continues to increase.

Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise Chart for CDNS
Estimate revisions ahead of a company's earnings release offer clues to the business conditions for the period whose results are coming out. This insight is at the core of our proprietary surprise prediction model -- the Zacks Earnings ESP (Expected Surprise Prediction).
The Zacks Earnings ESP compares the Most Accurate Estimate to the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the quarter; the Most Accurate Estimate is a more recent version of the Zacks Consensus EPS estimate. The idea here is that analysts revising their estimates right before an earnings release have the latest information, which could potentially be more accurate than what they and others contributing to the consensus had predicted earlier.
Thus, a positive or negative Earnings ESP reading theoretically indicates the likely deviation of the actual earnings from the consensus estimate. However, the model's predictive power is significant for positive ESP readings only.
A positive Earnings ESP is a strong predictor of an earnings beat, particularly when combined with a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), 2 (Buy) or 3 (Hold). Our research shows that stocks with this combination produce a positive surprise nearly 70% of the time, and a solid Zacks Rank actually increases the predictive power of Earnings ESP.
Please note that a negative Earnings ESP reading is not indicative of an earnings miss. Our research shows that it is difficult to predict an earnings beat with any degree of confidence for stocks with negative Earnings ESP readings and/or Zacks Rank of 4 (Sell) or 5 (Strong Sell).

Here's What You Should Know About Analysts' Price Targets
According to researchers at several universities across the globe, a price target is one of many pieces of information about a stock that misleads investors far more often than it guides. In fact, empirical research shows that price targets set by several analysts, irrespective of the extent of agreement, rarely indicate where the price of a stock could actually be heading.
While Wall Street analysts have deep knowledge of a company's fundamentals and the sensitivity of its business to economic and industry issues, many of them tend to set overly optimistic price targets. Are you wondering why?
They usually do that to drum up interest in shares of companies that their firms either have existing business relationships with or are looking to be associated with. In other words, business incentives of firms covering a stock often result in inflated price targets set by analysts.
However, a tight clustering of price targets, which is represented by a low standard deviation, indicates that analysts have a high degree of agreement about the direction and magnitude of a stock's price movement. While that doesn't necessarily mean the stock will hit the average price target, it could be a good starting point for further research aimed at identifying the potential fundamental driving forces.
That said, while investors should not entirely ignore price targets, making an investment decision solely based on them could lead to disappointing ROI. So, price targets should always be treated with a high degree of skepticism.

The market expects Cadence Design Systems (CDNS) to deliver a year-over-year increase in earnings on higher revenues when it reports results for the quarter ended September 2026. This widely-known consensus outlook is important in assessing the company's earnings picture, but a powerful factor that might influence its near-term stock price is how the actual results compare to these estimates.
The stock might move higher if these key numbers top expectations in the upcoming earnings report, which is expected to be released on October 26. On the other hand, if they miss, the stock may move lower.
While management's discussion of business conditions on the earnings call will mostly determine the sustainability of the immediate price change and future earnings expectations, it's worth having a handicapping insight into the odds of a positive EPS surprise.
This maker of hardware and software products for validating chip designs is expected to post quarterly earnings of $2.04 per share in its upcoming report, which represents a year-over-year change of +5.7%.
Revenues are expected to be $1.61 billion, up 20.3% from the year-ago quarter.
The consensus EPS estimate for the quarter has been revised 0.85% higher over the last 30 days to the current level. This is essentially a reflection of how the covering analysts have collectively reassessed their initial estimates over this period.
Investors should keep in mind that an aggregate change may not always reflect the direction of estimate revisions by each of the covering analysts.
Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise Chart for CDNS
Estimate revisions ahead of a company's earnings release offer clues to the business conditions for the period whose results are coming out. This insight is at the core of our proprietary surprise prediction model -- the Zacks Earnings ESP (Expected Surprise Prediction).
The Zacks Earnings ESP compares the Most Accurate Estimate to the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the quarter; the Most Accurate Estimate is a more recent version of the Zacks Consensus EPS estimate. The idea here is that analysts revising their estimates right before an earnings release have the latest information, which could potentially be more accurate than what they and others contributing to the consensus had predicted earlier.
Thus, a positive or negative Earnings ESP reading theoretically indicates the likely deviation of the actual earnings from the consensus estimate. However, the model's predictive power is significant for positive ESP readings only.
A positive Earnings ESP is a strong predictor of an earnings beat, particularly when combined with a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), 2 (Buy) or 3 (Hold). Our research shows that stocks with this combination produce a positive surprise nearly 70% of the time, and a solid Zacks Rank actually increases the predictive power of Earnings ESP.
Please note that a negative Earnings ESP reading is not indicative of an earnings miss. Our research shows that it is difficult to predict an earnings beat with any degree of confidence for stocks with negative Earnings ESP readings and/or Zacks Rank of 4 (Sell) or 5 (Strong Sell).
How Have the Numbers Shaped Up for Cadence?
For Cadence, the Most Accurate Estimate is higher than the Zacks Consensus Estimate, suggesting that analysts have recently become bullish on the company's earnings prospects. This has resulted in an Earnings ESP of +0.56%.
On the other hand, the stock currently carries a Zacks Rank of #2.

Does Earnings Surprise History Hold Any Clue?

Here's What You Should Know About Analysts' Price Targets
According to researchers at several universities across the globe, a price target is one of many pieces of information about a stock that misleads investors far more often than it guides. In fact, empirical research shows that price targets set by several analysts, irrespective of the extent of agreement, rarely indicate where the price of a stock could actually be heading.
While Wall Street analysts have deep knowledge of a company's fundamentals and the sensitivity of its business to economic and industry issues, many of them tend to set overly optimistic price targets. Are you wondering why?
They usually do that to drum up interest in shares of companies that their firms either have existing business relationships with or are looking to be associated with. In other words, business incentives of firms covering a stock often result in inflated price targets set by analysts.
However, a tight clustering of price targets, which is represented by a low standard deviation, indicates that analysts have a high degree of agreement about the direction and magnitude of a stock's price movement. While that doesn't necessarily mean the stock will hit the average price target, it could be a good starting point for further research aimed at identifying the potential fundamental driving forces.
That said, while investors should not entirely ignore price targets, making an investment decision solely based on them could lead to disappointing ROI. So, price targets should always be treated with a high degree of skepticism.
Here's Why There Could be Plenty of Upside Left in CDNS
There has been increasing optimism among analysts lately about the company's earnings prospects, as indicated by strong agreement among them in revising EPS estimates higher. Billings is a non-GAAP metric that is often called "cash revenue" because it shows how much money the company has collected from customers in a certain period. This is different from revenue, which must be recognized in pieces over the length of a contract.

Cadence Design Systems is extremely efficient at acquiring new customers, and its CAC payback period checked in at 11.3 months this quarter. The company's rapid recovery of its customer acquisition costs indicates it has a highly differentiated product offering and a strong brand reputation. These dynamics give Cadence Design Systems more resources to pursue new product initiatives while maintaining the flexibility to increase its sales and marketing investments.

Forecasted revenues by Wall Street analysts signal a company's potential. Predictions may not always be accurate, but accelerating growth typically boosts valuation multiples and stock prices while slowing growth does the opposite.

Cadence Reports Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results
Raising 2026 Revenue Outlook to 19% YoY Growth
Raising 2026 Non-GAAP EPS to $8.10 and Operating Cash Flow to $2 Billion
SAN JOSE, Calif. — July 27, 2026 — Cadence (Nasdaq: CDNS) today announced results for the second quarter of 2026.
•Revenue of $1.584 billion, compared to revenue of $1.275 billion in Q2 2025
•GAAP operating margin of 28.4%, compared to 19.0% in Q2 2025
•Non-GAAP operating margin of 45.5%, compared to 42.8% in Q2 2025
•GAAP diluted net income per share of $1.33, compared to $0.59 in Q2 2025
•Non-GAAP diluted net income per share of $2.11, compared to $1.65 in Q2 2025
•Quarter-end backlog was $8.1 billion and revenue expected to be recognized in the next 12 months from remaining performance obligations was $4.2 billion
“Cadence delivered an outstanding Q2 driven by broad-based strength and the accelerating demand for our AI-driven solutions across both Design for AI and AI for Design fronts,” said Anirudh Devgan, president and chief executive officer. “Cadence is leading the agentic AI transformation in semiconductor design with a healthy environment. We are uniquely positioned to capitalize on this massive TAM expansion opportunity as the only provider with agentic solutions spanning the full electronic system design flow.”
“Cadence delivered excellent results for the second quarter of 2026, with broad-based strength driving double-digit growth across all our businesses,” said John Wall, senior vice president and chief financial officer. “With a record backlog and continued business momentum, we are now raising our 2026 outlook to 19% revenue growth, non-GAAP operating margin to 44.25%, non-GAAP EPS to $8.10, and operating cash flow to $2 billion at the midpoint.”

Optical upgrades will support Openreach's wholesale offering
UK broadband provider Openreach has tapped Ciena to expand its high-capacity connectivity services for UK wholesale customers.
In an announcement today (October 7), Ciena confirmed that Openreach has been deploying Ciena's Waveserver 1.6Tbps coherent technology into its Optical Spectrum Extended Access (OSEA) portfolio. The deployment is underpinned by Ciena's WaveLogic 6 (WL6) technology.
Openreach is using the technology to provide its wholesale customers with tailored network solutions serving specialist locations such as cable landing stations (CLS), access and backhaul services to core intersect nodes and data centers.
The company, a subsidiary of UK telecoms giant BT, is currently building out its full fiber network across the country and is on course to hit 25 million locations by the end of this year.
Ciena notes that its solution includes the deployment of 400G and 800G client traffic over dedicated 1.6Tbps wavelengths, with a 2RU chassis supporting up to 32 x 400G services. In simple terms, Ciena claims this significantly expands the range of high-capacity services Openreach can offer.
Beyond this, Openreach has also introduced national 800G services for the first time and creates a clear path to even faster services as customers’ needs grow.
According to Ciena, its Waveserver technology gives Openreach's wholesale customers "more flexible, tailored options for services that need to carry very large amounts of data."
The company added that Openreach's wholesale customers that are using the telco's fiber network will be able to support high-capacity connections between data centers, private cloud networks for businesses, and connections between international cable landing stations and data centers.
In addition to this, there will be greater resiliency using different fiber routes across the UK, plus additional capacity to support growth in cloud services, online content and international subsea traffic.
“Demand for fast, reliable connectivity is growing rapidly. This investment shows how Openreach is strengthening its network to support wholesale customers across the UK,” said Nicolas Lemaitre, director of products, Openreach. “By using Ciena’s Waveserver and WL6 technology, we’re preparing our services for the next wave of digital growth, including increasing demand from AI applications and Critical National Infrastructure.”
Ciena's partnership with Openreach also extends to helping the broadband provider deploy, proactively monitor, and maintain its OSEA optical product.

Ciena Corporation (NYSE:CIEN) is positioned to benefit from the growing importance of optical networking as artificial intelligence infrastructure expands. As AI data centers scale, the need to move massive volumes of data between GPUs, servers, and data centers is driving demand for faster and higher-bandwidth optical connectivity.
Wall Street’s view on Ciena has shifted sharply. Targets were cut after earnings, then later raised following its 2029 outlook: see the analysis.
Connectivity within and between data centers remains a key challenge as hyperscalers build increasingly large AI clusters to support frontier large language models. According to Evercore ISI analyst Amit Daryanani, Ciena Corporation is well positioned to capitalize on this opportunity.
In a research note to investors on September 21, the analyst upgraded Ciena to an Outperform from In Line, buoyed by its prospects as a dedicated optical systems provider. The analysts also raised the stock’s price target to $550 from $375, insisting it offers an attractive way of gaining exposure to the optical networking space.
The analyst expects the company to be one of the biggest beneficiaries as the data center buildout fuels demand for optical networking systems and high-speed interconnects needed to enhance data transmission between and beyond data centers. It already provides systems capable of transporting massive amounts of data across networks, including between data centers.
Its technology is becoming increasingly important as AI clusters expand beyond individual facilities. Ciena has also introduced its Vesta 200 6.4T co-packaged optical engine, designed for high-density AI networking.
Backed by robust optical networking technology, the company expects revenue to grow at an annual rate of about 30% over the next three years, with adjusted gross margin reaching approximately 50% by fiscal 2029.
The combination of AI-driven data traffic, hyperscaler infrastructure spending, and the transition toward higher-speed optical connectivity could provide Ciena with a significant growth runway.
While the company is benefiting from strong AI-related demand, the stock remains vulnerable to earnings or valuation reset. The market is already pricing in a prolonged AI-driven optical networking boom. Given extremely high AI expectations, the stock could come under pressure if hyperscaler spending falls short.
Supply constraints could also limit the company’s ability to capitalize on strong demand fully. While industrywide constraints can support backlog growth, shortages of components and other inputs could delay converting orders into revenue.
Competition represents another risk. The attractive economics surrounding AI infrastructure could encourage additional investment from networking and optical technology providers, potentially increasing pricing pressure and limiting Ciena’s share of the market.
Insider Monkey database indicates that institutional positioning has been building up around the stock. The number of hedge funds holding Ciena Corporation shares rose to 81 in the second quarter, up from 73 in the first quarter. Arrowstreet Capital increased its stake in the company by 21% to $822.68 million, while AQR Capital Management increased its stake by 8% to $507.24 million.
Meanwhile, the amount of Ciena shares sold short dropped to 3.35 million as of August 31 from 3.71 million as of July 31, translating to a short interest of 2.36%.
Ciena Corporation offers investors exposure to the growing demand for optical networking amid robust AI data center buildout. The company’s optical systems and next-generation technologies could position it to benefit from the continued expansion of AI infrastructure.
The key question for investors is whether Ciena can translate the rapid expansion of AI-related networking demand into sustained revenue and margin growth without market expectations running too far ahead of fundamentals.

Did Analyst Upgrade Just Shift Ciena (CIEN) Investment Narrative?
Tue, October 20, 2026 at 7:19 PM CDT 4 min read
Ciena appointed Monika Fahlbusch as Executive Vice President and Chief People Officer on 12 October 2026, tasking her with leading the global People & Culture organization and using AI, data, and automation to evolve the group's people strategy.
The combination of Fahlbusch's background integrating AI into workforce decisions and Ciena's focus on optical networking for AI infrastructure ties talent management directly to the company's operational capacity and execution on long term demand.
We will look at how Ciena's investment narrative is shaped by this AI focused people leadership move alongside the bullish Evercore upgrade.

To own Ciena, you need to buy into a long AI network buildout and the company's ability to turn a record backlog and hyperscaler relationships into revenue and higher margins. The most important near term catalyst still sits in execution on optical deliveries and supply, not this appointment or any single quarter.
The biggest risk remains concentrated exposure to a small set of large cloud buyers and the possibility that orders slow or shift elsewhere, alongside ongoing supply constraints. Monika Fahlbusch's hire may help long term execution on talent and automation, but it does not materially change those immediate operational swing factors.
The Evercore upgrade is the clearest recent signal linked to this story. It highlights the same core thesis you as a shareholder would be underwriting, that Ciena's optical platforms and AI related networking exposure could support higher sales and earnings if demand for AI infrastructure and high capacity links stays healthy.
Where this intersects with catalysts is in execution risk. Analyst projections for sales and EPS growth assume Ciena converts backlog, maintains deep ties with hyperscalers, and manages costs effectively. Any shortfall in scaling capacity or product delivery would not just test those forecasts, it would also test the patience of a market that already views the stock as volatile.
Ciena's narrative projects US$13.0b revenue and US$3.0b earnings by 2029. That path assumes 29.4% yearly revenue growth and an earnings increase of about US$2.3b from US$654.4m today.

The most optimistic analysts were already pencilling in US$14.6b revenue and US$3.3b earnings by 2029 before this hire, compared with US$13.0b and US$3.0b in the baseline. Those views may shift as Monika Fahlbusch's AI focused people strategy plays out, so treat this appointment as a fresh reason to compare several narratives rather than accept any single forecast.

AI data center spending is splitting networking stocks into clear winners and laggards, and the gap between Ciena, Arista, and Cisco reveals which part of the network hyperscalers are actually racing to build.
Published October 19, 2026, 2:06pm ET · 3 min read
Market Movers desk. Editor: David Moadel.
Networking hardware is leading a broad technology rebound, and suppliers of optical links and Ethernet switches for AI data centers are drawing the biggest buying. By Monday afternoon, Ciena Corporation (NYSE:CIEN | CIEN Price Prediction) stock was up 4% to $347.48. Meanwhile, Arista Networks (NYSE:ANET) stock also climbed 4%, hitting $183.32 and keeping pace with the gain in Ciena shares.
Shares of Ciena and Arista are running well ahead of the wider technology group. The iShares U.S. Technology ETF (NYSEARCA:IYW) is up 1.29%. Large-cap tech is advancing at a similar pace, with the Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) also up 1.31%.
A sharp pullback in Ciena and Arista shares over the prior week came before the bounce. Hyperscaler spending on AI infrastructure remains the core support for Ciena and Arista. Both companies build the networks that move data between and inside AI data centers.
Supply Limits Keep Ciena’s Backlog Growing
Ciena’s fiscal Q3 2026 results showed adjusted EPS of $2.11 against a $1.73 consensus. The company’s revenue rose 37% year over year (YoY) to $1.67 billion.
Cloud providers did the biggest spending for Ciena, accounting for 53% of revenue on 82% YoY growth. Management raised its fiscal 2026 revenue guidance to $6.42 billion and issued a preliminary fiscal 2027 outlook calling for at least 30% revenue growth.
Strong demand also shows in Ciena’s backlog, as the company ended Q3 with $8.5 billion on the books and projects to exit fiscal 2026 with over $10 billion. During the earnings call, executives stated, “The demand is absolutely there.” Supply remains the limit, and management doesn’t projects the market to return to balance before 2028.
Optical Links and AI Switches Ride One Spending Wave
Ciena sells optical networking equipment that links data centers, while Arista and Cisco Systems (NASDAQ:CSCO) sell the switches and routers inside them. Pluggable optics were a standout, with Ciena’s pluggables revenue more than doubling YoY in Q3 as the WaveLogic 6 Nano ramped. Notably, CSCO stock is practically unchanged at $107.06 today, so it’s not keeping pace with CIEN and ANET today.
Arista’s EtherLink switches power Ethernet-based AI fabrics in hyperscale data centers. Management frames the Arista 2.0 strategy around networking. The company sees networking as the “central nervous system” for infrastructure, and EtherLink adoption has spread to a broader roster of cloud, AI and neocloud customers.
Scale-across networks, which connect AI training clusters spread over multiple data centers, are Ciena’s next growth leg. Its RLS HyperRail line system, co-created with hyperscalers, is on track for initial customer adoption by year-end and material revenue through 2027. Co-packaged optics offer another lever, with revenue projects to begin in 2027 and grow into 2028 for Ciena.
Improving operating leverage is showing up in Ciena’s results too, with adjusted gross margin expanding 450 basis points YoY to 46.4%. The company’s chief executive asserted in the earnings release that “AI continues to drive compounding waves of network investment.”
Ciena’s growth carries concentration risk, since two customers made up 41.7% of its Q3 revenue. Its outlook also assumes continued AI infrastructure spending by cloud providers, stable optical component supply and no material change to tariff policy.
Next quarter’s results could show whether Ciena can hit its fiscal Q4 2026 revenue guidance of $1.75 billion under tight component supply. Traders will be tracking whether Ciena and Arista shares keep outpacing the iShares U.S. Technology ETF and the Invesco QQQ Trust.
Long-term supplier agreements running through 2029 could ease Ciena’s bottleneck, though recent moves in its shares show how quickly sentiment can turn. Investors may want to hold smaller share stakes until the supply squeeze resolves.

Ciena's revenue could grow up to 40% as AI demand outstrips supply, says Bank of America
Bank of America expects Ciena Corporation (NYSE:CIEN), the optical networking equipment maker, to deliver revenue growth of 35% to 40% in the calendar year 2026 as demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure outstrips available supply.
The bank maintains a 'buy' rating on the shares with a $550 price target, supported by rising cloud-provider spending and expanding opportunities to connect data centres.
Bank of America forecasts revenue from direct cloud customers will grow 69% at the midpoint of its estimates, making this growth the main driver of Ciena's expected expansion.
The bank identifies Ciena's Reconfigurable Line System (RLS) and Waveserver platforms as key growth engines, as customers invest in optical infrastructure to move increasing volumes of data between cloud facilities.
Pluggable optical transceivers, which convert electrical signals into light for data transmission, are also expected to grow threefold year on year, while Meta's data centre out-of-band management business could generate $200 million in the calendar year 2026.
The outlook depends partly on Ciena's ability to deliver equipment into a market where supply constraints continue to limit shipments despite strong customer demand.
Bank of America also sees opportunities to sustain annual growth above 30% over the longer term through Hyper-Rail, connections between geographically distributed data centre clusters and new customers adopting data centre out-of-band management solutions.
These opportunities could expand Ciena's addressable market beyond traditional telecommunications networks as cloud operators build infrastructure to support increasingly demanding AI workloads.
An expected backlog of more than $10 billion provides an additional buffer, giving Ciena greater visibility into future demand and potential revenue conversion.
The bank's assessment points to a business with substantial growth opportunities, although the pace of expansion will depend on supply availability and the successful delivery of new customer programmes.

With a market cap of roughly $48.5 billion, it is one of the best-qualified names on our list of 9 New Contenders for the S&P 500 Index. Ciena (CIEN): Is the AI-Optical Boom Enough to Carry It Into the S&P 500?
The bull thesis puts forth the demand surge. AI data centers and telecom carriers are rushing to buy optical capacity. And this is reflected in the company's results. The record third-quarter revenue rose about 37%, and the stock has climbed roughly 98% over the past year. At a recent investor forum, management laid out a path toward 30% growth and much higher profit by fiscal 2029. If that bridge holds, the forward multiple near 40 times looks reasonable against the growth rate, and the trailing figure simply reflects earnings that are still in the early phase of catching up to revenue.
The bears find cyclicality a problem. Ciena sells hardware, and hardware demand moves in waves rather than a straight line. Component constraints can cap how much it ships in a given quarter. If there were a pause in the current data-center spending wave, it would hit revenue quickly. After a run this steep, there is little room for a demand air pocket, and the high trailing multiple assumes the profit ramp continues without a stumble. A single disappointing quarter on new orders could unwind a significant portion of the past year's gains, since so much optimism is already priced in at these levels.
In the past six months, the stock slid by -32 while the Insider Monkey Billionaire Index gained 11.6% over the same period.
The bottom line is that Ciena ticks every inclusion box. It is profitable and large. Its shares trade heavily. It does not need a profitability breakthrough the way the software names on our list do. Therefore, its case rests less on eligibility but more on whether the AI-optical boom keeps running long enough to justify the price. For the index committee, it is a clean, ready candidate. For an investor, the harder question is whether to buy a cyclical hardware supplier near the top of a sharp run, with its trailing multiple still remaining high.

Ciena Fell 40%—Now One Analyst Sees 50% Upside
Sam Quirke - MarketBeat - Wed Sep 23, 1:30PM CDT
Despite all the money pouring into the artificial intelligence boom, it feels like only a small handful of names have been consistent winners.
Plenty of companies quietly making that boom possible have been overlooked, their shares languishing while the giants soar. Ciena Corporation (NYSE: CIEN) is a good example.
Despite sitting right in the path of the AI wave, its stock has nonetheless tumbled more than 40% from its June high. However, that disconnect may be correcting itself.
After a punishing slide, the stock appears to have found a floor early this month and has started to turn higher, climbing around 17% in less than three weeks.
Even after its fall, Ciena is still up roughly 50% for the year, and the current bounce suggests investors are beginning to look again at a name they had written off. A well-timed vote of confidence from Wall Street this week has helped, making this a perfect time to ask if the market has been way too negative on Ciena’s prospects.
That vote of confidence came from Evercore ISI, with analyst Amit Daryanani upgrading Ciena to Outperform earlier this week and setting a $550 price target. From where the stock trades today, that's around 50% upside, and just as importantly, Daryanani's argument cuts to the heart of the bull case: that Ciena sits at one of the AI boom's most overlooked bottlenecks.
This bottleneck theory is simple. Amid all the noise about chips and computing power, far less attention goes to how that data actually moves around. Modern AI systems shuttle staggering volumes of information between and within data centers, and doing so fast enough has become a serious constraint on how powerful they can be. Daryanani pinpointed connectivity as an increasingly critical bottleneck to the pace of AI's advancement.
This is Ciena's world. The company specializes in optical networking, the high-speed connections that carry data over long distances and, increasingly, across the sprawling AI facilities springing up everywhere. As one of the few dedicated names in the field, it’s particularly well placed to benefit as those systems, and their data demands, keep growing.
The bullish case is more than a story, because the numbers behind it are seriously impressive. In its most recent quarterly report, released earlier this month, Ciena reported year-on-year revenue growth of 37% and earnings per share growth of 215%.
More telling still is the pipeline of future work. Ciena’s management pointed to a swelling order book, with its backlog expected to top $10 billion by the end of its financial year, giving it, and the market, solid visibility into future revenue.
Ciena is also pushing into new territory. Beyond its traditional strength in long-distance links, it's developing products that operate inside data centers themselves, chasing a market it believes could be worth many billions. With leading technology and a clutch of new products, it has several ways to win rather than relying on a single one.
None of this means the risks have vanished. The stock's steep fall from its June high and the volatility that followed remind us how quickly sentiment can turn on a name like this. The biggest worry is simply that the AI spending spree may not last, and Ciena's fortunes are tightly bound to how much the cloud giants keep investing, so any slowdown would hit its orders hard.
There’s also the matter of who its customers are. A handful of large clients account for a hefty slice of Ciena's revenue, with one customer alone making up close to 20%. Such concentration cuts both ways: it’s fine while those customers spend freely, but it would hurt if even one pulled back.
Weighing it up, Ciena makes a compelling case as an underappreciated way to play the AI infrastructure boom. It sits at a real bottleneck, its core business is growing fast, its order book offers rare visibility, and Wall Street is clearly leaning toward the upside.
The caution comes not from the bulls but from the setup itself. Ciena's shares remain volatile, its valuation demands strong growth for years to come, and expectations will likely stay high after this week's upgrade. That tension, between an early-stage turnaround and a business with a lot still to prove, is what keeps the stock finely balanced.
For those who believe the AI buildout has years left to run, though, Ciena increasingly looks like one of its more overlooked beneficiaries, and this week's upgrade is a clear sign that others are already catching on.

AI networking demand is lifting Arista Networks (NYSE:ANET | ANET Price Prediction), Cisco Systems (NASDAQ:CSCO) and Ciena (NYSE:CIEN), with shares of the optical supplier pulling far ahead of the two switching vendors. No company announcement accounts for the gain in Arista stock, which sits inside a broader bid across networking and optical equipment. That leaves the relative size of the three moves as the clearest signal of where the market sees demand outrunning supply.
Ciena stock is at $431.18, up 11% in midday trading, the largest gain of the three by a wide margin. Meanwhile, Arista Networks stock is at $214.34, up 4%, the smallest advance in the group. Cisco stock trades at $115.83, up 3%, landing between the other two.
For context, the iShares U.S. Technology ETF (NYSEARCA:IYW) is up 0.63%, a modest gain for the broader tech sector. At the same time, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSEARCA:SPY) is up 0.76%. Against those benchmarks, shares of Ciena, Arista and Cisco are each running well ahead of both the tech sector and the overall market, a sign that the buying is targeted at network equipment.
Bernstein Note Ties Networking to Optical
On October 1, Bernstein initiated coverage of Arista Networks with an Outperform rating and a price target of $250, arguing that networking and optical suppliers both benefit from AI infrastructure spending, with demand still running ahead of supply. That note is several days old and serves as background to the session. The detail that matters now is the note’s pairing of networking with optical, since shares of Ciena, the optical name in this group, are running hardest.
Arista Networks reported its second-quarter 2026 results in early August, with revenue growth of 37.7% from a year earlier. Demand across AI networking, data centers, campus and routing drove that growth, giving the company several engines working at once, and such breadth underpins Arista’s longer-term story, though the August report isn’t fresh news for the stock and doesn’t explain the latest buying on its own.
Transport Layer Shows Where Scarcity Sits
Inside data centers, Arista and Cisco sell the switches and routers that move traffic, while Ciena supplies the optical transport layer that carries traffic between those facilities. A buildout that adds computing capacity in more locations lifts transport demand before it lifts switching demand. That sequencing is the structural reason Ciena, Arista and Cisco shares don’t move in lockstep, even when the same AI theme is driving all three.
Ciena stock running several times harder than Arista stock points to the transport layer as the place where the market currently sees scarcity. Bernstein’s note collapsed exactly that distinction by grouping networking and optical suppliers together under one spending thesis. Arista stock is the smallest mover of the three, which complicates reading the session as a story about Arista itself.
Between those extremes, Cisco stock is advancing solidly, which suggests the bid extends across the equipment layer as a whole. The middle slot held by Cisco stock also gives the market a useful reference point, since a broad rally lifts the diversified networking giant while the sharpest gains collect in optical transport. Such a pattern fits a market rewarding AI infrastructure broadly. It reserves its biggest premium for the scarcest piece (we profiled seven of these non-chip AI suppliers, from networking to power and cooling, in a free report you can grab here).
Evidence that switching demand is tightening the way transport demand appears to be would tie the next move in Arista stock to the company specifically, and this session doesn’t supply it. Traders could look for signs that Arista faces the same supply pressure Bernstein described across networking and optical suppliers. Until then, Ciena stock remains a clearer expression of the transport scarcity the market is pricing.
Shareholders may want to keep an eye on whether Cisco stock continues advancing alongside Ciena and Arista, since a sustained broad rally would support the view that AI networking spending is lifting every tier of the equipment stack. A fade in CSCO stock while CIEN stock holds its gains would point to a narrower trade concentrated in optical transport. Either outcome may clarify whether the equipment rally has staying power beyond the optical names.
Ciena stock carries the most risk of the three if transport scarcity eases, since it is running so far ahead of the group, while Arista and Cisco shares are riding the same spending wave with smaller swings. Investors weighing their exposure should calibrate their holdings carefully given that a sector-wide bid across networking and optical equipment is driving all three stocks. Keeping their positions in any one of these names moderate limits how much their portfolios lean on a single tier of the AI networking buildout.

She has held senior positions at leading software, media and entertainment, and retail companies, most recently as Chief People Officer of Epic Games, with previous leadership roles at BMC Software, Salesforce.com, and PeopleSoft.
At Ciena, she will lead the company's global people strategy to support its continued growth, including advancing its people practices through technology, data, and automation.

What Was Ciena Telling You Before Its Stock Ran?
Tue, October 20, 2026 at 6:48 AM CDT 3 min read
Ciena (CIEN) stock returned 101.5% from October 16, 2025 to October 19, 2026, against 17.4% for the S&P 500. The run turned out to be about cloud providers and data centers ordering more of Ciena's optical networking gear than the company could ship. The rise began earlier, however. Shares had already risen 184% in the six months before that window opened. So what was Ciena telling investors before April 2025, when its shares still traded near $60?
On its fiscal Q4 2024 call, held December 12, 2024, management said "orders in the quarter were once again above revenue." Orders that outpace revenue move into backlog, representing sales booked but not yet shipped. By the end of that fiscal year, management placed Ciena's backlog at $2.1 billion.
This mattered because sales were standing still. Revenue in the quarter ended November 2, 2024, was $1.12 billion, flat from a year earlier. Management also said customers were working through accumulated inventory, so a reader could see orders stacking up behind a pause in shipments.

How Ciena's Orders Turned Into Sales In 2025
Management said on its fiscal Q1 2025 call, held March 11, 2025, that service providers had largely finished digesting that inventory. It also pointed to rapidly increasing demand for bandwidth driven by cloud connectivity. Reported sales were growing fast within two quarters. Revenue rose 23.6% from a year earlier in the quarter ended May 3, 2025. Growth reached 29.4% in the quarter ended August 2, 2025, and management said on the September 4, 2025, call that revenue came in above the top end of its guidance.
Ciena agreed on September 22, 2025, to acquire Nubis Communications, a maker of optical and electrical interconnects for AI workloads, to expand its business inside the data center. The December 2024 and March 2025 calls both took place before April 2025, while the sales gains and the Nubis deal occurred as the shares were already rising. The clearest signs were therefore public well before the measured window opened on October 16, 2025, and a reader who acted on them in early 2025 would have held the shares through both rises.
What Ciena Shareholders Are Paying For Now
Cisco Systems, Arista Networks and Broadcom all returned less than Ciena over the same window, with the best of them returning 57.0%. Ciena was also far more profitable than a year before: its operating margin was 18.1% in the quarter ended August 1, 2026, against 6.2% a year earlier. Management said direct cloud provider revenue grew over 80% in that quarter. You now pay 74.7 times Ciena's earnings over the last twelve months, against 22.9 for the S&P 500.
The sign from December 2024 is still there. On its fiscal Q3 2026 call, held September 3, 2026, management said orders were again well ahead of sales, and Ciena ended that quarter with $8.5 billion in backlog. Management expects backlog of more than $10 billion by the end of fiscal 2026. Ciena's backlog is the figure to watch in the fiscal fourth quarter report, expected on or around December 9, 2026.

Jim Cramer Likes Ciena (CIEN) but Another Optical Stock Holds His Attention
During the October 5 lightning round of Mad Money, a caller asked Jim Cramer about Ciena Corporation (NYSE:CIEN). He replied:
I think Ciena's very good. I happen to like optical. You know, the one that I had liked for the Club was Corning. I'm waiting for it to come down to be able to get back in. It never seems to come in.
His reluctance to chase Corning is not new. In September, Cramer gave a more specific reason for waiting, despite describing the business as good.
